sla — SLA Compiler Plugin (Overview)

Zig 0.17This plugin is built with Zig 0.17: the 0.17 branch builds with Zig 0.17 and passes the Zig unit tests; the old 0.14.1 branch is kept unchanged.

sa_plugin_sla is the Sla language compiler and tooling plugin for Safe ASM (SA): it provides Sla → SA / SAB compilation, and exposes the sla capability segment and a set of CLI commands to the host SA environment. This page only gives positioning and entry points; for SLA's syntax, types, and ownership rules, see the "SLA Language Reference" chapter, and for command-line details, see the "Command-Line Reference" chapter.

Positioning

  • Capability segment: sla; no plugin dependencies; permissions are read/write/create in the project directory, the HOME/PATH/SA_* environment variables, and permission to spawn /opt/zig/zig.
  • The project is in active development before 1.0. Current position (2026-11-15): SA text is the only production path — the frontend emits .sa text, which the host Flattener then parses; SAB structured artifacts have been sealed as an optimization direction (tag sab-sealed-2026-11-15), opt-in only. The SAB path has no SA compatibility fallback (removed since 2026-09-28); uncovered features error explicitly.
  • Maturity snapshot (measured locally on 2026-07-07): the frontend check sa sla check passes 306/313 demos, and end-to-end sa sla build-exe is about 76% (239/313); for concrete metrics, the repository's docs/roadmap_status_cn.md is authoritative.
  • Sla directly imports SA's top-level sa_std package (such as @import "sa_std/io/print.sai"), and uses compiler-managed lifetime cleanup by default — user-facing .sla needs no explicit release.

Main commands at a glance

CommandDescription
sa sla init [path]Create a minimal project skeleton (sa.mod + src/main.sla)
sa sla check <file>Lexical/syntax/type checking, without emitting SA assembly
sa sla build <file>Compile to a verified .sa file
sa sla build-exe <file> -o outBy default, emits .sa via the SA text path and compiles it to an executable; only an explicit --test-backend sab takes the direct SAB path
sa sla sab build|workspace|disasmSAB direct compilation / workspace member compilation / disassembly (short alias slab ...)
sa sla test <file>Compile a test file and run it under sa test, with backend selectable among auto/sab/sa
Repeat buildsWhen the source is unchanged, build / build-exe / test no longer recompile everything: the frontend freshness gate reuses artifacts in .sla-cache/fresh/ by the content hash of the dependency closure (root file + all imported modules + contract files + the sibling sa.mod), skipping the whole frontend pipeline; on the SA side, the build-exe cache covers all emission paths (including the CGU path with --jobs), and sla no longer appends --jobs auto to SA commands by default. SLA_NO_FRESHNESS_CACHE=1 disables the frontend gate; for the principle and magnitude, see the FAQ's "Performance and Optimization Expectations" page.
NoteThis plugin's docs/ directory holds over a hundred documents (architecture, the SAB pipeline, roadmap status, benchmarks, the language specification, a tutorial series, etc.); the repository is authoritative for all of them. Known limitations include: &mut T not yet introduced (currently &self covers reads and writes, with the SA Referee as backstop), some language features still taking compatibility fallback paths, and not all demos/rosetta samples passing end to end.
